profile.reading:
The building at 3101 Western Avenue in Seattle, Washington, is a seven storey office building dating from 1984 in the Belltown neighbourhood near Elliott Bay. It carries the name CTI Biopharma in OpenStreetMap, and CTI Biopharma was a real Seattle biopharmaceutical company. It developed treatments for haematologic cancers, cancers of the blood and bone marrow, and brought its lead drug pacritinib, sold under the brand name Vonjo, to market for myelofibrosis, a rare bone marrow disorder. In 2023 the Swedish pharmaceutical company Sobi, Swedish Orphan Biovitrum, acquired CTI Biopharma, and the ctibiopharma.com domain now redirects visitors to Sobi's United States site.

The data centre tag on this building is a late addition by a single mapper and does not describe the building's use. The edit history is unambiguous. The footprint was imported in May 2013 by the SeattleImport account from King County GIS and data.seattle.gov as an unnamed building carrying only a street address. A mapper added the name CTI Biopharma and an office tag in October 2016, another added the seven storey count a week later, a third changed the building type to office in 2021, and a fourth added a 1984 construction date and a link to the King County Assessor parcel record in December 2022. Only on 11 December 2023 did a mapper add the telecom data centre tag, in a changeset commented updating information regarding this location and sourced to aerial imagery and local knowledge. That same edit removed the office tag which six years of previous mapping had established.

Neither aerial imagery nor a passing observation can establish that an occupied office tower is a data centre, and nothing published about CTI Biopharma or about Sobi's acquisition of it suggests the company ever ran a colocation or wholesale data centre business at this or any other address. A life sciences company of this size keeps its own internal IT equipment, a server room supporting corporate systems, laboratory instruments and research computing. That is an ordinary feature of almost every occupied office building and is not what the term data centre means in this registry.

This entry is recorded as a correction rather than padded with unrelated infrastructure detail. The building is corporate office and laboratory space. No IT load, utility power service, standby generation, on-site generation, technical floor area or data centre ownership figure is recorded here, because none exists to record. Registries assembled by harvesting OpenStreetMap telecom tags without review carry a long tail of rows shaped exactly like this one, where a single well meant edit converts a named office building into a counted facility and every downstream copy of the data repeats the error.
profile.research_note: Confirmed mistag 2026-09-05 via full OSM version history on way/223783259. Seven versions: v1 2013-05-31 SeattleImport (King County GIS import, unnamed building); v2 2016-10-02 seattlefyi adds name=CTI Biopharma and office=yes; v3 2016-10-09 Omnific adds building:levels=7; v4 2021-09-19 Wim L sets building=office; v5 2022-12-18 Ballard OpenStreetMap adds start_date=1984 and the King County Assessor parcel link; v6 2023-12-11 0x4rk0 adds telecom=data_center and drops office=yes, changeset 145010430 commented "Updating information regarding this location", source "aerial imagery;local knowledge"; v7 2024-03-27 TheDutchMan13 adds addr:state. The data centre claim rests entirely on that one 2023 edit with no operator or documentary source. Prior confirmation retained that ctibiopharma.com redirects to sobi.com/usa/en, corroborating the 2023 Sobi acquisition. No capacity or power figures asserted.

reading.body:
This entry does not describe a data centre. The building at 3101 Western Avenue in Seattle is a seven-storey office and laboratory building dating from 1984, occupied by CTI Biopharma until its 2023 acquisition by Swedish pharmaceutical company Sobi. A single mapper added the data centre tag on 11 December 2023 without operator confirmation, documentary source, or published capacity figure, removing the office tag that six years of prior mapping had established. No IT load, power service, standby generation, technical floor area, or data centre ownership has been published for this address.

The research note confirms the mistag through complete OpenStreetMap version history. The building carried only a street address and no data centre designation from its import in 2013 through December 2022. The sole claim rests on that one changeset attributed to aerial imagery and local knowledge, with no operator source, no capacity assertion, and no technical specification of any kind. A life sciences company of this scale maintains server rooms for internal corporate and research systems, a feature of nearly every occupied office building and distinct from the colocation and wholesale data centre business that this registry tracks.

This campus does not merit consideration in decisions about AI infrastructure. Washington state has 46 mapped facilities but only two with published capacity figures totalling 60 MW, neither of which is this building. No power specification, utility agreement, or operator announcement connects this address to AI workload or grid constraint.
